concepts.title: Simple Interest on the Principal
concepts.definition: Under simple interest every period charges the same fixed fraction of the original principal only; earlier interest never joins the base, so the charge grows in a straight line.
concepts.key_idea: Interest rides on the opening principal alone, so equal periods cost equal interest.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.2, SI = P x r x t / 100 with fixed fraction of the principal

concepts.title: Maturity Amount at Simple Interest
concepts.definition: The amount repaid at simple interest is the principal plus the straight-line interest collected over the whole term, returned as one maturity figure.
concepts.key_idea: Amount is just the principal wearing its interest on top.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.2, simple interest accumulation on banking products

concepts.title: Compound Interest Earned
concepts.definition: Compound interest adds each period's interest back into the base, so interest itself starts earning interest and the debt or deposit grows geometrically. The interest charge is the grown amount minus the original principal.
concepts.key_idea: Interest joins the base every period; the charge is growth minus the starting sum.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.2, A = P (1 + r/100)^n and CI = A - P

solution_steps.explain: the accumulated amount after n compounding periods

concepts.title: Accumulated Amount under Compound Interest
concepts.definition: The amount after n compounding periods is the principal scaled by the factor one plus the periodic rate raised to the nth power, the compounded maturity value of the deposit or loan.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply once by the whole growth factor instead of stepping year by year.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.2, A = P (1 + r/100)^n accumulation formula

solution_steps.explain: the compounded amount

concepts.title: Annual Equivalent and Effective Rate
concepts.definition: A nominal rate compounded m times a year earns more than its face value; the annual equivalent rate is the single yearly rate that would pile up the same money, and it beats the nominal rate whenever compounding is more frequent than annual.
concepts.key_idea: Compound m times, strip the principal, and you have the true yearly rate.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.3, AER = (1 + r/m)^m - 1, effective rate exceeds nominal for intra-year compounding, bond coupons half yearly or quarterly

concepts.title: Present Value by Discounting
concepts.definition: Discounting runs compounding backwards: the present value of an amount A falling due after n years is the sum that, invested today at rate r, would grow into A. Future money is worth less today by the discount factor.
concepts.key_idea: Divide by the growth factor instead of multiplying by it.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.4, PV = A / (1 + r/100)^n, discounting reverses compounding

solution_steps.action: build the discount-deflating factor
solution_steps.explain: the same compounding factor used forward

solution_steps.action: divide the future amount by the factor
solution_steps.explain: discounting strips the interest that has not happened yet

concepts.title: Net Present Value of a Cash Flow
concepts.definition: The net present value discounts every future cash inflow back to today and subtracts the initial cost. A positive NPV means the project creates value and approves the investment in capital budgeting; a negative one rejects it.
concepts.key_idea: Discount the inflows, subtract the outlay; positive approves, negative rejects.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.4, NPV as sum of present values of inflows minus initial cost, capital budgeting decisions

solution_steps.explain: one plus rate per 100 raised to the years

solution_steps.action: bring the future inflow back to today
solution_steps.explain: for a stream, this discounting is repeated and the pieces added

solution_steps.action: subtract the initial cost
solution_steps.explain: the value created or destroyed today

concepts.title: Future Value of an Annuity
concepts.definition: An annuity is a run of equal periodic payments. Piled up at the end, each payment compounds for the periods it survives, and the total is the future value of the stream, the arithmetic behind recurring deposits.
concepts.key_idea: Every equal payment compounds for a different number of periods; the annuity factor does all the adding.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.5, FV = A ((1 + r)^n - 1) / r, recurring deposit and FVAF tables

solution_steps.action: convert the quoted annual rate into the per-period rate
solution_steps.explain: divide by the number of compounding periods per year

solution_steps.action: grow the annuity numerator
solution_steps.explain: one plus i raised to n, minus one

solution_steps.action: multiply the payment by the annuity factor
solution_steps.explain: payment times growth over i is the accumulated corpus

concepts.title: Present Value of an Annuity
concepts.definition: The present value of an annuity prices a stream of equal future payments in today's money: each payment is discounted from the period it lands in, and the discounted pieces sum to what the whole stream is worth now, as tabulated in PVAF tables.
concepts.key_idea: Discount each equal payment to today; the annuity factor collapses the sum.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.5, PV = A (1 - (1 + r)^(-n)) / r and PVAF tables

concepts.title: Sinking Fund Deposits
concepts.definition: A sinking fund accumulates equal periodic deposits so that with compound interest they reach a target corpus on a fixed date. The required deposit is the target share of the annuity factor's inverse.
concepts.key_idea: Work the future value formula backwards: target divided by the annuity factor, per period.
concepts.textbook_ref: am11_011_financial_mathematics.txt, section 11.5, a sinking fund accumulates equal deposits toward a target corpus

solution_steps.explain: one plus i to the n minus one

solution_steps.action: scale the target by the inverse annuity factor
solution_steps.explain: target times i over growth is the equal deposit

concepts.title: Electricity Bill Slabs
concepts.definition: Utility bills charge slab-wise: the first block of units is billed at one rate and every unit beyond it at the next rate, plus any fixed charge. Units come from power in kilowatts times hours, and checking the meter reading against the slabs exposes overcharging.
concepts.key_idea: Split the units at the slab boundary, price each block at its own rate, then add the fixed charge.
